newsitem.title: CANADA: Bouyant charters suggest strong Asia-US cargo peak.
newsitem.headline: Bouyant charters suggest strong Asia-US cargo peak.

text.p: Airfreight carriers serving the U.S. import-export market are seeing a strong fourth quarter peak in the making, says an industry analyst.
A number of leading indicators suggest capacity will be tight, Brian Clancy, a principal in the MergeGlobal air cargo consultancy, said in a telephone interview from Arlington, Virginia.
One is the existence this year of a "vibrant" fourth quarter market for air cargo charters from Asia to the U.S., said Clancy.

"Whenever the charter market is active, it means shippers moving inventory for the Christmas selling period are picking up signals there is going to be more demand than they maybe originally anticipated," Clancy said.
U.S. import traffic peaks in the fourth quarter as U.S. consumers go on their annual Christmas buying binge, said Clancy.
Retail sales last year never quite lived up to expectations, said Clancy. Air carriers were caught with too much capacity in the transpacific market in particular. Charter demand plunged.

"Last year's problem was that the fall peak ex-Asia was not as big as it normally was, given an onslaught of capacity put in by scheduled carriers, and that really collapsed the rate structure", he said.
"This year, the market is a lot tighter than it was last year, and the charter market is being stimulated," he said,
Second quarter U.S.economic indicators reported strong gross domestic product growth, real income growth and minimal inflation, all positives for consumer confidence.
"There has been more disposable income and retail sales to come extent have picked up somewhat," said Clancy.
"Most retailers are anticipating a much better year than last year than last year, and that is now reflecting itself in the air pipeline."
Clancy said that demand from Europe to the U.S. also is stronger this year, resulting in a "somewhat tight" capacity situation for the forthcoming peak.
On the export side, outbound North American air freight traffic tends to be less peak-driven, particularly on the Pacific.
In recent years, demand has been strong and fairly well spread, thanks to Asian economic growth which shows no sign of slackening, said Clancy.

"What is good news for most operators of freighter aircraft in particular is that the import market is also strong, so you basically have decent bi-directional strength in the Far East market." --Air Cargo Newsroom Tel +44 171 542 7706 Fax +44 171 542 5017
